xml/parse#

XML text read into a tree (#144):

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let feed = ParsedXml(text).document();
feed.root().attribute("version");
for feed.root().children("item") -> item {
    item.text("title");
}

Description#

XML text read into a tree (#144):

The parser does not validate and knows no DTD: a DOCTYPE with an internal subset is refused and an external one is never fetched, so the only entities are the five predefined ones and character references. Elements may nest 256 deep and a document may hold a million events (tags, texts, comments, instructions) unless told otherwise. Namespaces are resolved: names carry their namespace, and xmlns attributes become the names' bindings rather than attributes, so what the tree writes reads back the same. A document that is not well formed is InvalidXml at its character offset.
